story.title: Gadi Eisenkot Assigned to Form New Israeli Government After Elections
story.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has officially tasked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government following the inconclusive results of the October 28 elections. Eisenkot, who leads an anti-Netanyahu alliance, has up to six weeks to negotiate a coalition capable of securing a parliamentary majority. The process is expected to be challenging, with potential alliances being politically sensitive.

explore_lenses.label: Why did Herzog choose Eisenkot first?
explore_lenses.title: More recommendations, but no assured majority
explore_lenses.summary: The mandate gives Eisenkot the first attempt to assemble a government; it does not make him prime minister or resolve the parliamentary deadlock.

claims.text: Official election results gave Likud 27 seats and Eisenkot's Yashar! 21; no party won a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.
During consultations, factions representing 67 MKs recommended Eisenkot, compared with 46 for Netanyahu; a seven-MK faction made no recommendation.
Herzog said the recommendation totals did not by themselves settle who could form a government because of vetoes between and within blocs, so he held further talks before selecting a candidate.

points: Official election results gave Likud 27 seats and Eisenkot's Yashar! 21; no party won a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.
During consultations, factions representing 67 MKs recommended Eisenkot, compared with 46 for Netanyahu; a seven-MK faction made no recommendation.
Herzog said the recommendation totals did not by themselves settle who could form a government because of vetoes between and within blocs, so he held further talks before selecting a candidate.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The formal recommendation count is not the same as a binding coalition commitment or a guaranteed confidence-vote majority.

explore_lenses.label: Can Eisenkot build a 61-seat coalition?
explore_lenses.title: Arab-party backing is pivotal and contested
explore_lenses.summary: Eisenkot's potential route to a majority relies heavily on the Joint List and Ra'am, but some prospective non-Arab partners oppose a government dependent on those parties.

claims.text: The Joint List won 11 seats and Ra'am won 8, for 19 combined; Yashar!, Be'Yahad, the Democrats and Yisrael Beitenu together hold 48 seats.
The President's Office lists both the Joint List and Ra'am among the factions that recommended Eisenkot.

Yisrael Beitenu leader Avigdor Liberman said he would not support a government relying on Arab parties, including through their abstention in a confidence vote, arguing that it would harm security and ultimately return Netanyahu to power.

Eisenkot's stated requirement that coalition members support mandatory military or civil service creates another potential obstacle to an agreement with ultra-Orthodox parties seeking to preserve military exemptions.

explore_lenses.label: What happens if coalition talks fail?
explore_lenses.title: A timed mandate followed by another decision
explore_lenses.summary: Eisenkot has a defined negotiating window, after which the president must either give another MK an opportunity or conclude that no government can be formed at that stage.

claims.text: Under Basic Law: The Government, the first designated MK has 28 days to form a government; the president may grant extensions totaling no more than 14 additional days.
If that attempt ends unsuccessfully, the law requires the president within three days either to assign the task to another willing MK or notify the Knesset speaker that no government can be formed.
The new 26th Knesset is scheduled to convene and swear in its members on November 10, 2026, while Netanyahu and his cabinet remain in caretaker office until a coalition is formed.

story_report.summary: President Isaac Herzog has assigned former military chief Gadi Eisenkot the task of trying to assemble Israel’s next government after the October 28 election produced no clear winner. Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to negotiate a coalition able to command support in the 120-seat Knesset, while Benjamin Netanyahu and his cabinet remain in caretaker office until a new government is formed.

sections.heading: Election Results Leave Fragmented Knesset
sections.body: Official results gave Netanyahu’s Likud 27 seats and Eisenkot’s Yashar! 21, leaving both well short of a majority in the 120-member Knesset. During presidential consultations, factions representing 67 MKs recommended Eisenkot, while 46 recommended Netanyahu and a seven-member faction did not make a recommendation. Herzog said those totals alone could not determine who was capable of forming a government because of vetoes across and within the political blocs.

sections.heading: Arab Parties and Service Policy Complicate Talks
sections.body: The Joint List and Ra’am hold 19 seats combined and were among the factions recommending Eisenkot; Yashar!, Be’Yahad, the Democrats and Yisrael Beitenu hold 48 seats together. But Yisrael Beitenu leader Avigdor Liberman has said he will not support a government dependent on Arab parties, including through abstentions in a confidence vote. Eisenkot’s requirement that coalition members back mandatory military or civil service could also impede an agreement with ultra-Orthodox parties seeking to retain military exemptions.

sections.heading: Israeli Law Sets Coalition Deadlines
sections.body: Under Basic Law: The Government, Eisenkot’s initial mandate lasts 28 days, and the president can grant extensions totaling up to a further 14 days. If his effort fails, the president must within three days either give the task to another willing MK or tell the Knesset speaker that no government can be formed. The 26th Knesset is scheduled to convene and swear in members on November 10, 2026.

unresolved.text: The recommendations received by Eisenkot do not constitute binding coalition commitments or guarantee a confidence-vote majority.
It remains unclear whether Eisenkot will pursue formal Arab-party participation, outside support, or an alternative arrangement involving ultra-Orthodox parties.
If Eisenkot cannot form a government, whether Netanyahu receives a later mandate or Israel moves toward another election will depend on subsequent talks and presidential decisions.

related_stories.title: ANC Faces Significant Defeat in South Africa's Local Elections
related_stories.summary: The African National Congress (ANC) is projected to receive around 30% of the vote in South Africa's recent local elections, marking its lowest electoral performance to date. With over 80% of ballots counted, the party's share is significantly lower than its results in previous elections, indicating a continued decline for the once-dominant political force. The election results are expected to lead to coalition negotiations in major cities like Johannesburg and Tshwane.
